title: Sustainable Financing Partnership
summary: MBRHE reports that AI credit and eligibility models automate housing-loan assessment and remove manual approval bottlenecks. The chapter does not measure AI’s separate effect.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: MBRHE reports that AI models evaluate housing-loan eligibility and priority using credit, income and social criteria. It identifies logistic regression, decision trees and ensemble models trained with historical approvals and credit-bureau data. The models are described as removing manual approval bottlenecks within a service integrated with Emirates Islamic Bank. Full deployment is dated to Q1 2025. Bank financing, interest subsidies, APIs and digital identity also contribute to the overall program. Its loan volume, budget savings and workload totals do not isolate the models’ contribution.
purpose: Reduce manual work and delays in housing-loan eligibility assessment.
system: MBRHE AI housing-loan credit and eligibility assessment
deployer: Mohammed Bin Rashid Housing Establishment and Emirates Islamic Bank

ratings.reason: The source reports that AI automates credit and eligibility evaluation and removes manual approval bottlenecks. This supports a qualitative processing-efficiency claim; the wider program’s 30% workload reduction is not assigned to AI alone.

The source reports that automated eligibility evaluation helps applicants move through approval more quickly. The rating covers that claimed convenience, not the financing partnership’s total loan volume or household welfare.

ai_role.statement: Trained credit and social-vulnerability models automate eligibility assessment. The chapter reports fewer manual approval bottlenecks but does not isolate AI’s effect from financing and workflow changes.

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The reported outcomes are attributed to the submitting project, not an independent outcome evaluation by ITU.
evidence.title: Use Case 8 Sustainable Financing Partnership

produced_by: Credit-risk and eligibility models integrated into housing-loan assessment
must_hold: Historical approvals, credit-bureau information, income and social-eligibility data
Bank-system APIs and digital identity access integrated with the eligibility workflow

headline: AI assesses housing-loan eligibility in Dubai

revisions.change: Added the sourced case with separate benefit depth, beneficiary, evidence confidence, and outcome status assessments.

claim_basis: The makers' report is on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
